text.p: Molson Breweries said Wednesday that its net income for the second quarter of fiscal 1997 was C$63.6 million, up C$3.0 million over the same period last year.
Sales revenue for the quarter was slightly down at C$593.6 million, compared to C$594.0 million in the second quarter last year, the company said in a statement.
For the six months ending October 1, net income was C$123.0 million, up C$2 million from last year. Sales revenue for the year to date was C$1.18 billion versus C$1.19 billion in 1995.
Molson said its volume for the first six months declined 3.5 percent compared to last year. Volume for the quarter fell 1.9 percent over last year.

The company's market share of domestic beer in Canada for the first half of the fiscal year was 47.1 percent compared to 47.8 percent last year, reflecting a higher share in Ontario offset by lower share in Quebec and British Columbia.
For the quarter, Molson's market share of domestic beer in Canada was 47.0 percent compared to 47.8 percent last year.
Year-to-date exports to the U.S. were 3.5 percent lower than last year.
Molson Breweries said it is continuing talks with U.S. brewer Adolph Coors Co regarding a long-term agreement to brew and sell Coors beer in Canada.
Last week, Molson and Coors reached an interim agreement to brew and market Coors Light and Original Coors at least through June 30, 1997.

The interm deal came two weeks after an arbitration panel tore up Molson's contract for Coors beer in Canada. The panel said Molson breached its licensing deal by allowing Miller Brewing to buy a 20 percent stake in Molson Breweries without Coors' consent in 1993.
The panel also ordered Molson to pay damages to Coors that could total tens of millions of dollars. The exact amount will determined at a hearing scheduled for May 19, 1997.

"As a result, the estimate of monies due to Coors is not reasonably determinable at this time and the six month financial results do not reflect any provision for amounts related to this ruling," Molson said.
